title: Modern Indian History
summary: From Vasco da Gama to 1947: British expansion and the Governor-Generals, the Revolt of 1857, reform movements, early Congress, the Gandhian movements, revolutionaries, and the newspapers and books of the freedom struggle. It is the most-asked history block in SSC CGL. Expect 1–2 questions per shift, mostly event–year, reform–Governor-General and founder–organisation pairs.

subtopics.title: Europeans in India & British Expansion
subtopics.concept:
**Arrival of the Europeans**

| Power | Key date | Facts |
|---|---|---|
| **Portuguese** | **1498** | **Vasco da Gama** landed near **Calicut** (Kappad), ruler Zamorin; **Albuquerque** took **Goa (1510)** |
| Dutch | 1602 | VOC; Pulicat, Masulipatnam; lost to the English at **Bedara (1759)** |
| **English** | **31 Dec 1600** | East India Company charter from **Elizabeth I**; first permanent factory at **Surat (1613)** |
| Danish | 1616 | Tranquebar, Serampore |
| **French** | **1664** | Compagnie des Indes under **Colbert**; **Pondicherry (1674)**; Dupleix was the key governor |

**Decisive battles**

| Battle | Year | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Plassey** | **23 June 1757** | **Robert Clive** defeated **Siraj-ud-Daulah**; Mir Jafar's treachery |
| Wandiwash | 1760 | Eyre Coote defeated the French (Lally) — ended French hopes (3rd Carnatic War) |
| **Buxar** | **22 Oct 1764** | Hector Munro defeated **Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula & Shah Alam II** → **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**: **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar & Orissa to the Company |
| Anglo-Mysore wars | 1767–1799 | Four wars; **Tipu Sultan** killed at **Srirangapatna (1799)** |
| Anglo-Maratha wars | 1775–1818 | 1st ended by **Treaty of Salbai (1782)**; 3rd war ended Peshwa rule |
| Anglo-Sikh wars | 1845–49 | Punjab annexed (1849) |

**Governors-General & Viceroys — one fact each**

| Name | Remember for |
|---|---|
| **Warren Hastings** | First Governor-General of Bengal (Regulating Act 1773); Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784, founded by William Jones) |
| **Cornwallis** | **Permanent Settlement (1793)**; "father of the civil services" |
| **Wellesley** | **Subsidiary Alliance** (1798); Hyderabad first to sign |
| **William Bentinck** | First **Governor-General of India** (Charter Act 1833); **abolished sati (1829)**; English Education Act 1835 (Macaulay) |
| Dalhousie | First railway **Bombay–Thane (16 April 1853)**, telegraph, Wood's Despatch (1854) |
| **Canning** | Last Governor-General & **first Viceroy (1858)** |
| **Lytton** | Delhi Durbar 1877; **Vernacular Press Act 1878** |
| **Ripon** | "Father of **local self-government**" (1882); **Ilbert Bill** (1883); first synchronous **census 1881** |
| Dufferin | INC founded (1885) |
| **Curzon** | **Partition of Bengal (1905)**; Ancient Monuments Preservation Act (1904) |
| Hardinge II | Capital shift to **Delhi** and annulment of partition announced (1911) |
| Mountbatten | Last Viceroy; first Governor-General of independent India; **C. Rajagopalachari** was the last (and only Indian) Governor-General |

tricks.title: Plassey then Buxar — "57 buys, 64 seals"
tricks.body: **1757 Plassey** gave the British a foothold (Clive vs Siraj); **1764 Buxar** sealed control (three Indian rulers beaten) and brought the **Diwani (1765)**.

example.q: Which battle was fought against the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II?

tricks.title: Governor-General reforms — "Cornwallis Settles, Wellesley Subsidises, Bentinck bans Sati, Ripon Rules locally"

mistakes: Warren Hastings = first GG of **Bengal**; William Bentinck = first GG of **India**; Canning = first **Viceroy**.
Ilbert Bill is **Ripon's** era, not Curzon's.
The English first factory was at **Surat**; Calicut is linked with Vasco da Gama.

subtopics.title: Revolt of 1857 and Peasant & Tribal Uprisings
subtopics.concept:
**Revolt of 1857**

| Point | Fact |
|---|---|
| Immediate cause | **Enfield rifle** cartridges said to be greased with cow and pig fat |
| First spark | **Mangal Pandey**, **Barrackpore**, 29 March 1857 |
| Outbreak | **Meerut, 10 May 1857** — sepoys marched to Delhi |
| Symbolic leader | **Bahadur Shah Zafar** (exiled to **Rangoon**) |
| Viceroy then | **Canning** |
| Result | **Government of India Act 1858** — Crown rule; Queen's Proclamation read at Allahabad, 1 Nov 1858 |

**Centre → Indian leader → British officer**

| Centre | Indian leader | British suppressor |
|---|---|---|
| Delhi | Bahadur Shah Zafar, General **Bakht Khan** | John Nicholson, Hudson |
| **Kanpur** | **Nana Saheb**, Tantia Tope | Colin Campbell |
| **Lucknow** | **Begum Hazrat Mahal** | Colin Campbell |
| **Jhansi** | **Rani Lakshmibai** | **Hugh Rose** |
| **Jagdishpur (Bihar)** | **Kunwar Singh** | William Taylor, Vincent Eyre |
| Faizabad | Maulvi Ahmadullah | — |
| Bareilly | Khan Bahadur Khan | — |

**Peasant & tribal movements**

| Movement | Year | Region | Leader / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Santhal Hul** | 1855–56 | Rajmahal hills (Jharkhand) | **Sidhu & Kanhu** |
| **Indigo revolt** | 1859–60 | Bengal | Play *Neel Darpan* by Dinabandhu Mitra |
| **Munda Ulgulan** | 1899–1900 | Chotanagpur | **Birsa Munda** |
| Moplah | 1921 | Malabar (Kerala) | Linked to Khilafat |
| **Bardoli Satyagraha** | 1928 | Gujarat | **Vallabhbhai Patel** — earned the title **"Sardar"** |
| Tebhaga | 1946 | Bengal | Sharecroppers demanded two-thirds of the crop |

tricks.title: 1857 pairs — "Kanpur Nana, Lucknow Lady, Jhansi Rani, Bihar Kunwar"
tricks.body: **K**anpur–**N**ana Saheb · **L**ucknow–Begum Hazrat Mahal (the Lady) · **J**hansi–Rani Lakshmibai · **B**ihar (Jagdishpur)–Kunwar Singh, the 80-year-old.

example.q: Kunwar Singh led the revolt of 1857 in which region?

mistakes: The revolt **broke out at Meerut** (10 May); Barrackpore saw Mangal Pandey's earlier act.
Rani Lakshmibai was defeated by **Hugh Rose**, not Colin Campbell.
Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to **Rangoon**, not the Andamans.

subtopics.title: Socio-Religious Reform Movements
subtopics.concept:
| Organisation | Year | Founder | Remember for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Atmiya Sabha | 1815 | Raja Ram Mohan Roy | Precursor of Brahmo Samaj |
| **Brahmo Sabha / Samaj** | **1828** | **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** | Monotheism; campaign against **sati** |
| Young Bengal | 1820s | **Henry Vivian Derozio** | Radical students of Hindu College |
| Tattvabodhini Sabha | 1839 | Debendranath Tagore | — |
| **Prarthana Samaj** | 1867 | **Atmaram Pandurang** (Bombay) | M.G. Ranade joined |
| **Satyashodhak Samaj** | **1873** | **Jyotirao Phule** | Book ***Gulamgiri*** (1873); rights of lower castes |
| **Arya Samaj** | **1875** | **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** (Bombay) | ***Satyarth Prakash***; "Back to the Vedas"; Shuddhi |
| **Theosophical Society** | 1875 | **Madame Blavatsky & Col. Olcott** (New York) | Headquarters shifted to **Adyar, Madras**; Annie Besant later led it |
| Aligarh Movement | 1875 | **Sir Syed Ahmad Khan** | Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College → **AMU (1920)** |
| **Ramakrishna Mission** | **1897** | **Swami Vivekananda** | Belur Math; Chicago speech 1893 |
| SNDP Yogam | 1903 | **Sree Narayana Guru** (Kerala) | "One caste, one religion, one God" |
| Self-Respect Movement | 1925 | **E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar)** | Tamil Nadu |

**Laws linked to reformers**

| Law | Year | Reformer behind it |
|---|---|---|
| Bengal Sati Regulation | 1829 | Ram Mohan Roy (Bentinck) |
| **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act** | **1856** | **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** |
| Age of Consent Act | 1891 | Behramji Malabari |
| Sarda Act (child marriage restraint) | 1929 | Har Bilas Sarda |

tricks.title: 1875 — the year of three
tricks.body: **Arya Samaj** (Dayanand), **Theosophical Society** (Blavatsky–Olcott) and the **Aligarh MAO school** (Syed Ahmad Khan) all date to **1875**.

example.q: Which two of these began in the same year — Arya Samaj, Brahmo Samaj, Theosophical Society, Ramakrishna Mission?

tricks.title: Founder hooks
tricks.body: **R**am Mohan = **R**eform of sati (Brahmo, 1828) · **D**ayanand = **D**iscover the Vedas (Arya) · **P**hule = **P**eople of lower castes (Satyashodhak) · **V**ivekananda = **V**edanta service (RK Mission, 1897).

mistakes: Ramakrishna Mission was founded by **Vivekananda** (1897), not Ramakrishna Paramahamsa himself.
Theosophical Society was founded in **New York**, then moved to Adyar.
Widow Remarriage Act 1856 = **Vidyasagar**; sati abolition 1829 = Ram Mohan Roy's campaign.

subtopics.title: Congress, Moderates & Extremists (1885–1916)
subtopics.concept:
**Milestones**

| Year | Event | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **1885** | INC founded | Bombay, 28 Dec; **A.O. Hume**; 72 delegates |
| 1905 | **Partition of Bengal** | Announced by **Curzon**; effective **16 Oct 1905** → **Swadeshi & Boycott** movement |
| **1906** | **Muslim League** | Founded at **Dhaka**; Calcutta INC session (Dadabhai Naoroji) first used the word **Swaraj** |
| **1907** | **Surat split** | Moderates vs Extremists (president Rash Behari Ghosh) |
| 1909 | **Morley–Minto Reforms** | **Separate electorates** for Muslims |
| 1911 | Delhi Durbar | Partition annulled; capital to shift from Calcutta to **Delhi** |
| **1916** | **Lucknow Pact** | Congress–League unity; Moderates & Extremists reunite |
| 1916 | **Home Rule Leagues** | **Tilak** (April, Belgaum) and **Annie Besant** (Sept, Madras) |

**Moderates vs Extremists**

| Moderates | Extremists (Lal–Bal–Pal) |
|---|---|
| Dadabhai Naoroji ("Grand Old Man"; **drain theory** in *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India*) | **Lala Lajpat Rai** (Punjab) |
| **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** (Gandhi's political guru; Servants of India Society 1905) | **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** — "Swaraj is my birthright"; *Kesari* (Marathi), *Mahratta* (English); *Gita Rahasya* |
| Pherozeshah Mehta, Surendranath Banerjee | **Bipin Chandra Pal** (Bengal); Aurobindo Ghosh |

**Early revolutionaries:** Chapekar brothers (1897, Poona); **Khudiram Bose** & Prafulla Chaki (Muzaffarpur, 1908); **India House, London** (Shyamji Krishna Varma); **Ghadar Party (1913)** — **Lala Har Dayal**, Sohan Singh Bhakna, HQ **Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco**; Komagata Maru (1914).

tricks.title: Five-six-seven-nine: "Split, League, Split, Separate"
tricks.body: **1905** Bengal split → **1906** Muslim League → **1907** Congress split (Surat) → **1909** separate electorates (Morley–Minto).

example.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced by —

mistakes: Gokhale (Moderate) was Gandhi's political guru, not Tilak.
Lucknow Pact (1916) was between the **Congress and the Muslim League**.

subtopics.title: Gandhian Era & Road to Independence (1915–1947)
subtopics.concept:
**Timeline (the most-asked table in modern history)**

| Year | Event | Key fact |
|---|---|---|
| 1915 | Gandhi returns from South Africa | **9 January** (Pravasi Bharatiya Divas) |
| **1917** | **Champaran Satyagraha** | **Bihar**, indigo (tinkathia); first satyagraha in India; invited by Raj Kumar Shukla |
| 1918 | Ahmedabad mill strike; **Kheda** satyagraha | First hunger strike; Kheda = peasant revenue relief (Patel) |
| 1919 | **Rowlatt Act** & **Jallianwala Bagh** | Massacre on **13 April 1919 (Baisakhi)** by **General Dyer**; **Tagore renounced his knighthood**; Hunter Committee |
| 1920 | **Khilafat & Non-Cooperation** | Launched 1 Aug 1920; approved at Calcutta special session, ratified at Nagpur |
| 1923 | Swaraj Party | **C.R. Das & Motilal Nehru** |
| 1928 | **Simon Commission** | All-white; "Simon Go Back"; **Lala Lajpat Rai** died after lathi charge in Lahore |
| **1929** | **Lahore Session** | President **Jawaharlal Nehru**; **Purna Swaraj** resolution; **26 Jan 1930** first Independence Day |
| **1930** | **Dandi March / Civil Disobedience** | **12 March** from **Sabarmati** → Dandi on **6 April**; 78 satyagrahis, about 385 km |
| 1931 | **Gandhi–Irwin Pact** (5 March); **Karachi Session** | Karachi (president **Vallabhbhai Patel**) — resolution on **Fundamental Rights & Economic Policy**; Gandhi attended the **2nd Round Table Conference** |
| 1932 | Communal Award → **Poona Pact** | **Gandhi & B.R. Ambedkar**, 24 Sept 1932 — reserved seats for depressed classes in joint electorates |
| 1935 | Government of India Act | Provincial autonomy; basis of much of the Constitution |
| 1939 | Tripuri session | Subhas Bose re-elected, then resigned; formed **Forward Bloc** |
| 1940 | August Offer; Individual Satyagraha | **Vinoba Bhave** first individual satyagrahi |
| 1942 | **Cripps Mission** (March); **Quit India** (**8 Aug**) | Resolution at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**; slogan **"Do or Die"** |
| 1943 | **Azad Hind Government** | Proclaimed by **Subhas Bose** in **Singapore** on 21 Oct 1943; INA slogan "Delhi Chalo" |
| 1946 | RIN mutiny; **Cabinet Mission**; Direct Action Day (16 Aug) | Interim Government 2 Sept 1946 |
| 1947 | **Mountbatten Plan** (3 June); Indian Independence Act (18 July) | Independence 15 Aug 1947 |

**Revolutionaries of the 1920s–30s**

| Event | Year | People |
|---|---|---|
| **Kakori train action** | 9 Aug 1925 | **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan** (HRA) |
| HSRA formed | 1928 | Bhagat Singh, **Chandrashekhar Azad** (Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi) |
| Central Legislative Assembly bomb | **8 April 1929** | **Bhagat Singh & Batukeshwar Dutt** |
| Chittagong armoury raid | 1930 | **Surya Sen** |
| Execution | **23 March 1931** | Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev (Martyrs' Day) |

example.q: Gandhi's first hunger strike in India was during —

tricks.title: Session presidents that repeat in exams
tricks.body: **Lahore 1929 = Jawaharlal** (Purna Swaraj) · **Karachi 1931 = Patel** (Fundamental Rights) · **Tripuri 1939 = Bose**. "J-P-B" from 29 to 39.

tricks.title: Dandi numbers
tricks.body: **12 March** start · **6 April** salt law broken · **78** marchers · about **385 km** (240 miles) · from **Sabarmati Ashram**.

mistakes: Purna Swaraj was adopted at **Lahore (1929)**; the first Independence Day was celebrated on **26 Jan 1930**.
Poona Pact was between **Gandhi and Ambedkar**, not Gandhi and Irwin.
Quit India was launched in **Bombay** (Gowalia Tank Maidan), 8 August 1942.
The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed in **Singapore**, not Rangoon or Tokyo.

subtopics.title: Newspapers, Journals & Books of the Freedom Era
subtopics.concept:
**Newspaper / journal → founder or editor**

| Paper | Language | Person |
|---|---|---|
| *Bengal Gazette* (1780) | English | **James Augustus Hicky** — first newspaper in India |
| *Sambad Kaumudi* | Bengali | Raja Ram Mohan Roy |
| *Kesari* / *Mahratta* | Marathi / English | **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** |
| *Indian Opinion* | English, Gujarati & others | Gandhi (South Africa) |
| *Young India*, *Navajivan*, *Harijan* | English / Gujarati | **Gandhi** |
| ***Al-Hilal*** (1912) | Urdu | **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** |
| *Comrade* | English | Mohammad Ali Jauhar |
| *Bande Mataram* | English | Aurobindo Ghosh (with Bipin Chandra Pal) |
| *New India* | English | **Annie Besant** |
| *Mooknayak* (1920) | Marathi | **B.R. Ambedkar** |
| *National Herald* (1938) | English | Jawaharlal Nehru |

**Book → author**

| Book | Author |
|---|---|
| *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* | **Dadabhai Naoroji** (drain theory) |
| *Anandamath* (source of "Vande Mataram") | **Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay** |
| *Gita Rahasya* | Tilak (written in **Mandalay** jail) |
| ***Hind Swaraj*** (1909) | **Mahatma Gandhi** |
| *The Discovery of India* | Jawaharlal Nehru (Ahmednagar Fort jail) |
| *Gulamgiri* | Jyotirao Phule |
| *Why I Am an Atheist* | Bhagat Singh |
| *Neel Darpan* | Dinabandhu Mitra |
| *Annihilation of Caste* | B.R. Ambedkar |

tricks.title: Gandhi's papers — "YNH"
tricks.body: **Y**oung India · **N**avajivan · **H**arijan (plus *Indian Opinion* from South Africa). Anything else in the options is someone else's paper.

example.q: Which of these was NOT edited by Gandhi — Young India, Harijan, Kesari, Navajivan?

tricks.title: Jail-written classics
tricks.body: Tilak → *Gita Rahasya* in **Mandalay**; Nehru → *Discovery of India* in **Ahmednagar Fort**.

mistakes: *Al-Hilal* = Abul Kalam Azad; *Comrade* = Mohammad Ali Jauhar.
*Anandamath* is by Bankim Chandra; the anthem *Jana Gana Mana* is by Tagore.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "In which year…" or "arrange in chronological order" with Gandhian-era events.
pyqPatterns.approach: Memorise the 1917–1947 timeline table; for ordering, fix the first and last events and use elimination.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Permanent Settlement, Subsidiary Alliance, sati, Vernacular Press Act, local self-government, partition of Bengal.
pyqPatterns.approach: One fact per GG from the table; watch the 'first GG of Bengal / India / first Viceroy' trap.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: "… was founded by", "… was edited by", "who wrote …".
pyqPatterns.approach: Use the founder-hook mnemonics; 1875 is the year of Arya Samaj and the Theosophical Society.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Jagdishpur, Delhi with a name to match.
pyqPatterns.approach: "Kanpur Nana, Lucknow Lady, Jhansi Rani, Bihar Kunwar".

solvedExamples.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Rowlatt Satyagraha
2. Arrival of the Simon Commission
3. Champaran Satyagraha
4. Gandhi–Irwin Pact
solvedExamples.solution: Champaran **1917** → Rowlatt Satyagraha **1919** → Simon Commission **1928** → Gandhi–Irwin Pact **1931**. Order: 3, 1, 2, 4.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Champaran is Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, so it must come first → only A and C remain; Rowlatt (1919) is before Simon (1928) → A.

solvedExamples.q: Which of the following pairs of Governor-General/Viceroy and measure is **NOT** correctly matched?
options: Lord Canning — First Viceroy of India
solvedExamples.solution: The **Ilbert Bill (1883)**, which allowed Indian judges to try Europeans, came under **Lord Ripon**. Curzon is linked with the partition of Bengal (1905). The other three pairs are correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Ripon is the 'liberal' Viceroy — both the local self-government resolution and the Ilbert Bill belong to him.

solvedExamples.q: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the Revolt of 1857 at —
solvedExamples.solution: **Begum Hazrat Mahal** of Awadh led the rising at **Lucknow** and proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr ruler. Kanpur – Nana Saheb; Jhansi – Rani Lakshmibai; Faizabad – Maulvi Ahmadullah.

solvedExamples.q: The resolution on **Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy** was adopted by the Indian National Congress at its 1931 session held at —
solvedExamples.solution: The **Karachi session (March 1931)**, presided over by **Vallabhbhai Patel**, adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme and endorsed the Gandhi–Irwin Pact. Lahore (1929) adopted Purna Swaraj.

practice.q: The **Battle of Plassey**, in which Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, was fought in —
practice.solution: Plassey was fought on **23 June 1757**. 1764 = Buxar; 1761 = Third Panipat; 1799 = death of Tipu Sultan.

practice.q: The **Diwani** of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa was granted to the East India Company by the —
practice.solution: After Buxar, Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani (right to collect revenue) through the **Treaty of Allahabad (1765)**. Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War; Srirangapatna (1792) the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

practice.q: The **Subsidiary Alliance** system was introduced by —
practice.solution: **Lord Wellesley** (1798–1805) made Indian rulers keep British troops at their own cost and accept a British Resident; the Nizam of Hyderabad signed first (1798).

practice.q: The **Permanent Settlement** of land revenue in Bengal (1793) was introduced by —
practice.solution: **Lord Cornwallis** fixed revenue permanently with the zamindars in 1793. It is also called the Zamindari system.

practice.q: The practice of **sati** was declared illegal in 1829 during the tenure of —
practice.solution: The **Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII) of 1829** was passed by **Lord William Bentinck**, supported by the campaign of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

practice.q: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at **Kanpur**?
practice.solution: **Nana Saheb**, adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II, led the revolt at Kanpur with Tantia Tope. Kunwar Singh – Jagdishpur (Bihar); Begum Hazrat Mahal – Lucknow; Khan Bahadur Khan – Bareilly.

practice.q: The **Arya Samaj** was founded in 1875 by —
practice.solution: **Swami Dayanand Saraswati** founded the Arya Samaj in **Bombay (1875)**. He wrote *Satyarth Prakash* and gave the call 'Back to the Vedas'.

practice.q: The **Satyashodhak Samaj** (1873), which worked for the rights of the lower castes, was founded by —
practice.solution: **Jyotirao Phule** founded the Satyashodhak Samaj ('Society of Truth-seekers') in 1873 in Maharashtra and wrote *Gulamgiri* the same year.
practice.shortcut: **P**hule = **P**eople of the lower castes; year **1873** = Gulamgiri year.

practice.q: The **Partition of Bengal** (1905) was carried out by which Viceroy?
practice.solution: **Lord Curzon** announced the partition, which took effect on **16 October 1905** and triggered the Swadeshi movement. It was annulled in **1911** under Lord Hardinge.

practice.q: The Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at its session held at **Surat** in —
practice.solution: The **Surat split** took place in **December 1907**. The two groups reunited at Lucknow in **1916**.
practice.shortcut: 5-6-**7**-9: Bengal split, League, **Congress split**, separate electorates.

practice.q: The **Champaran Satyagraha** (1917), Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, took place in present-day —
practice.solution: Champaran is in **Bihar**. Gandhi went there on Raj Kumar Shukla's request to take up the grievances of indigo cultivators under the **tinkathia** system.
practice.shortcut: **C**hamparan = first letter of the chain C-A-K; indigo in Bihar.

practice.q: Who renounced his knighthood in protest against the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** of 1919?
practice.solution: **Rabindranath Tagore** gave up the knighthood conferred on him in 1915 by writing to the Viceroy (Lord Chelmsford) in May 1919. Gandhi later returned his Kaiser-i-Hind medal.
practice.shortcut: Only a 'Sir' could renounce a knighthood → Sir Rabindranath.

practice.q: The **Purna Swaraj** resolution was adopted at the Lahore session of the Congress (1929) presided over by —
practice.solution: **Jawaharlal Nehru** presided over the **Lahore session (December 1929)**, which declared complete independence as the goal; 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Independence Day.

practice.q: Gandhi began the **Dandi March** from Sabarmati Ashram on —
practice.solution: The march started on **12 March 1930** and reached Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law on **6 April 1930**. 5 March 1931 is the Gandhi–Irwin Pact.
practice.shortcut: **12** March start, **6** April finish — start is always the March date.

practice.q: The **Poona Pact (1932)** on the representation of the depressed classes was signed between —
practice.solution: After the **Communal Award** (1932), Gandhi fasted in Yerawada jail. The **Poona Pact** with **B.R. Ambedkar** replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in joint electorates.

practice.q: The slogan **'Do or Die'** was given by Gandhi during the —
practice.solution: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' on **8 August 1942** at **Gowalia Tank, Bombay**, when the Quit India resolution was passed.
practice.shortcut: 1942 = last big push → last-chance slogan 'Do or Die'.

practice.q: The headquarters of the **Ghadar Party** (Yugantar Ashram) was located in —
practice.solution: The Ghadar Party (1913), led by **Lala Har Dayal** and **Sohan Singh Bhakna**, was run from **Yugantar Ashram in San Francisco**, USA, and published the weekly *Ghadar*.
practice.shortcut: Ghadar = Indians on the **US Pacific coast** → San Francisco.

practice.q: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the **Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)** on 21 October 1943 at —
practice.solution: The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed in **Singapore**. The INA's HQ later moved to Rangoon; Bose had earlier worked from Berlin.

practice.q: The Urdu weekly ***Al-Hilal*** (1912) was started by —
practice.solution: **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** launched *Al-Hilal* from Calcutta in 1912. Mohammad Ali Jauhar edited *Comrade*.
